evidence: ZnSe epilayers were grown on semi-insulating GaAs (100) substrates by metalorganic atomic layer epitaxy (MOALE) using dimethylzinc (DMZn) and hydrogen selenide (H2Se) source gases with a substrate temperature of 350°C. The substrate is exposed alternatively to the DMZn and H2Se precursor streams by rotating its position among the inlet tubes. Excess DMZn gas is subsequently purged away by H2 gas for 6 seconds. ZnSe is formed when H2Se reacts with the adsorbed DMZn and 2CH4 is liberated.
